records.content_text:
A straight line is also called a straight angle. A straight angle is equal to $180^{\circ}$. If a straight line is formed by more than one angle, the sum of those angles will be $180^{\circ}$. We say the angles are **supplementary angles**.

In the first diagram, the two angles are supplementary angles, because they form a straight line:

$$
\hat{P}_1 + \hat{P}_2 = 180^{\circ}
$$

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-024.png]

We can also say that the two angles in the diagram above are **adjacent angles**. Adjacent angles are next to each other. Two adjacent angles share the same vertex and they also share one common arm.

In the second diagram below, $\hat{M}_1$ and $\hat{M}_2$ have the same vertex, but they do not share a common arm.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-15-025.png]

$\hat{M}_1$ and $\hat{M}_2$ are not adjacent angles, because they do not share a common arm.

records.prompt_text:
Consider the diagram given below. You are given the following information:

- $\overset{\leftrightarrow}{ST}$ is a straight line
- $a = 65^{\circ}$
- $b = 68^{\circ}$
- $c = x^{\circ}$

Diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_050.png

What is the value of $x$?
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Read the given information and consider the diagram carefully.

Begin the answer by writing down the facts you know.

The angles must have a sum of $180^{\circ}$, because they form a straight line.

$$
a + b + c = 180^{\circ}
$$

Step 2: Substitute all the values, including the unknown value, $x$.

$$
\begin{align}
a + b + c & = 180^{\circ} \\
65^{\circ} + 68^{\circ} + x & = 180^{\circ} \\
\end{align}
$$

Step 3: Solve the equation.

$$
\begin{align}
a + b + c & = 180^{\circ} \\
65^{\circ} + 68^{\circ} + x & = 180^{\circ} \\
133^{\circ} + x & = 180^{\circ}\\
x & = 180^{\circ} - 133^{\circ}\\
\therefore x & = 47^{\circ} \\
\end{align}
$$

You could now complete the diagram by replacing the $x$.

Completed diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-1_029.png

records.content_text:
When we refer to lines and line segments we can use different notations:

- $\overline{EF}$ means the line segment from point $E$ to point $F$.
- $\overset{\leftrightarrow}{EF}$ means the line through points $E$ and $F$.
- Most of the time we simply write $EF$ for the line through point $E$ and point $F$ and also for the line segment from point $E$ to point $F$.

records.prompt_text:
### Exercise 15.3: Calculate angles on a straight line

7. In the diagram below, line $YZ$ is a straight line with angles labelled above and below it.

Diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-0_016.png

Find the values of $x$ and $y$, giving reasons for your answer. (Remember to check your answers.)
records.answer_text:
All of the angles above $YZ$ add up to $180^{\circ}$:

$$
\begin{align}
x + 65^{\circ} + 60^{\circ} & = 180^{\circ} \quad(\text{angles on a straight line}) \\
x + 125^{\circ} & = 180^{\circ}\\
x & = 180^{\circ} - 125^{\circ}\\
\therefore x & = 55^{\circ} \\
\end{align}
$$

In the same way, all of the angles below $YZ$ add up to $180^{\circ}$:

$$
\begin{align}
26^{\circ} + 82^{\circ} + 35^{\circ} + y & = 180^{\circ} \quad(\text{angles on a straight line}) \\
143^{\circ} + y & = 180^{\circ} \\
y & = 180^{\circ} - 143^{\circ} \\
\therefore y & = 37^{\circ} \\
\end{align}
$$

Completed diagram source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/sv-qb-jss1-15-1_007.png

The angles in a full turn (revolution) must add up to $360^{\circ}$. This is a good way to check your answers:

$$
\begin{align}
55^{\circ} + 65^{\circ} + 60^{\circ} + 26^{\circ} + 82^{\circ} + 35^{\circ} + 37^{\circ} & = 360^{\circ} \\
\end{align}
$$

records.content_text:
An angle is the amount of turn between two straight lines that have a common end point, called the vertex of the angle.

We use a protractor to measure angles in degrees. Always estimate an angle before you measure it, so you can check whether your answer seems correct.

Different types of angles used in this chapter include:

- acute angle: between $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$
- right angle: $90^{\circ}$
- obtuse angle: between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$
- straight angle: $180^{\circ}$
- reflex angle: between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$
- revolution: $360^{\circ}$

A straight line is also called a straight angle. A straight angle is equal to $180^{\circ}$.

If a straight line is formed by more than one angle, the sum of those angles will be $180^{\circ}$. We say the angles are supplementary angles.

Adjacent angles are next to each other. Two adjacent angles share the same vertex and one common arm.

When two lines cross each other, we say they are intersecting lines.

Two intersecting straight lines form vertically opposite angles, which have the same vertex and are on opposite sides of the vertex. Vertically opposite angles are equal.

Parallel lines are always the same distance apart, and are indicated using arrow symbols.

A transversal intersects two or more parallel lines.

There are three types of angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal:

- Corresponding angles are in matching positions on the parallel lines and the transversal, and make an F shape. Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.
- Co-interior angles are inside the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal. They make a U shape. Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary and add up to $180^{\circ}$.
- Alternate angles are inside the parallel lines, but on different sides of the transversal. They make an N shape. Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.
